title: Compute Frugality Initiative — Cycle-based velocity and gating plan
creator: Maya Flores
description: Objective: Reduce per-token cost for tiered hosted workloads by 18–25% over the next three cycles by coordinating batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization rollouts. This initiative stitches together engineering experiment grids, console rollout controls, and PM/Design gating so that savings are measurable and quality regressions are prevented. Scope: discover highest-impact workloads, run controlled experiments (A/B) with live traffic shadowing, build rollout policies in Console for automatic fallbacks, and produce a repeatable playbook for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate per-token cost reduction >= 18% on the targeted fleet within release window
No >2% regression in end-user latency P95 after batching changes for production traffic
Quality guardrail in place: prompt-level eval set with automatic regression alerts
Console rollout policy supports canary/auto-fallback and exposes token-level cost delta
Quantization variants validated on representative models with documented accuracy delta and a fallback path
comments: 2026-02-10 — Kickoff: aligned PM, Eng (runtime & infra), Design, and Research. Confluence plan created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CF/Compute+Frugality+Initiative
2026-02-22 — Eng proposed experiment grid (batch sizes x prefetch policy x quant level). Initial estimate 21 pts; trimmed to 13 after scoping to two priority workloads.
2026-02-28 — Design review: added a Console cost-delta card in rollout flow; DES flagged visual complexity for low-privilege users (DES-1101 opened).

2026-03-03 — Research ran offline eval on 4 models; quantization at 4-bit with per-layer calibration shows median quality delta 0.6% on our eval set. Action: add automated post-deploy sampling for subjective QA.
2026-03-09 — GitHub PR for runtime batching heuristics opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482 — requested performance microbenchmarks from infra team.
2026-03-11 — Product review: agreed gating thresholds (cost >18% AND quality delta <1% on eval). Assigned Lukas to lead rollout orchestration and canary policies.
decision_log: Prefer a conservative default batching heuristic (latency-SLO-aware) rather than aggressive batching by default to avoid P95 regressions for latency-sensitive customers.
Adopt per-model quantization profiles published in the model catalog and surfaced in Console; runtime will auto-fallback to fp16 when accuracy regressions are detected.
KV cache prefetching will be enabled behind a config flag with sampling; full rollout requires no increase in error surface (HTTP 5xx) during canary.
Trade-off: deeper quantization yields larger cost savings but increases QA burden. We prioritize quant levels that are validated by research for each model family.
risks: Quality regression in long-tail prompts not captured by existing eval set
Coupling batching heuristics too tightly to hardware profiles could reduce portability to Dedicated/Private deployments
Insufficient observability on token-level accounting for early canaries could mask regressions
Rollout orchestration complexity may delay ship if console changes slip
mitigations: Expand eval prompt set with customer-provided examples and fuzzing; run nightly regression checks
Ensure runtime exposes a hardware-agnostic batching API and document model-specific flags for Dedicated customers
Add temporary high-verbosity tracing for first 48h of canary and a dashboard alert for token-cost anomaly
Prioritize a minimal viable Console control for canary + auto-fallback; move advanced UX to a follow-up cycle
metrics_and_signals: Per-token cost (hosted fleet) — baseline vs experiment
Latency P95 and P99 per route
Quality regression rate (eval-set delta & human-sampled feedback)
Rollback rate and Canary success ratio
